title: Count the Number of Houses at a Certain Distance II
summary: Given positive integers n, x, and y, find the number of house pairs for each distance k (1 to n) where k is the minimum streets needed to travel between any two houses.
statement: Given positive integers n, x, and y, find the number of house pairs for each distance k (1 to n) where k is the minimum streets needed to travel between any two houses. Return a 1-indexed array where each element represents the count of such pairs for the corresponding distance.
constraints: Houses one through n form a path plus one extra undirected x-y street, with n up to 100,000 and x possibly equal to y.
Count ordered pairs of distinct houses by shortest-path distance.
Return n buckets in O(n) time; index d-1 corresponds to distance d.
reference_solution:
def count_house_pair_distances_large(n,x,y):
    if abs(x-y)<=1:return [2*value for value in reversed(range(n))]
    cycle=abs(x-y)+1;reduced=n-cycle+2
    answer=[2*value for value in reversed(range(reduced))]+[0]*(n-reduced)
    cycle_counts=[cycle*2]*(cycle//2)
    if cycle%2==0:cycle_counts[-1]=cycle
    cycle_counts[0]-=2
    for index,value in enumerate(cycle_counts):answer[index]+=value
    if x>y:x,y=y,x
    for tail in (x-1,n-y):
        if not tail:continue
        length=tail+cycle//2;maximum=4*min((cycle-3)//2,tail);mirror=length-(1-cycle%2)
        extra=[maximum]*length;extra[0]=extra[1]=0
        if cycle%2==0:extra[-1]=0
        for index,value in enumerate(range(4,maximum,4)):
            extra[index+2]=value;extra[mirror-index-1]=value
        for index in range(1,tail+1):extra[index]+=2
        if cycle%2==0:
            for index in range(cycle//2,cycle//2+tail):extra[index]+=2
        for index,value in enumerate(extra):answer[index]+=value
    return answer
